name: Wendy Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Walk me through your shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 27, and I lead a chat and phone team in a contact centre. My two-year college diploma got me in, but listening to calls taught me the harder part. I use AI tools every day to summarise chats and spot missing account details, and I check the customer record before the reply goes out.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you enjoy, and what follows you home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like fixing a bad handoff between the bot and an agent. I hate when the dashboard says a call was solved but the customer rings back. My pay is typical for this job, and I rent alone; four months of expenses saved lets me sleep, but I still notice a weak rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team the helper can shave a minute off a routine chat, and that is fine. I'd still put the messy complaint on my own screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I like the tools, but a plateau means there is no magic new role waiting for me. My four months of savings make that more of a career question than a rent emergency.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep supervising the chat queue and use the approved AI summary tool each day. In the first year I'll save the time from routine summaries for coaching agents on difficult cases, then check whether satisfaction scores actually rise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, though a little bored by the thought that nothing bigger changes. I want to keep learning whether the software improves or not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you check a summary?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I record the same complaint in plain words before and after the tool's summary. If it drops the reason for the refund, I put that detail back before anyone reads it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much room do your savings give you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I rent a small flat alone and keep four months of expenses untouched. I can afford a short experiment with my time, not a careless job change.

say: I'd welcome **small time savings** on routine chats, provided an agent checks each summary against the customer record.
I'd keep **messy complaints** on an agent's screen.
think: I see no **new role** appearing just because a helper improves.
My **four-month reserve** keeps the question from becoming a rent crisis.
do: Use the **approved summary tool** on routine chats.
Coach agents on **difficult cases** with the saved minutes.
Check **satisfaction scores** before calling the change useful.
feel: **Calm**, with curiosity about whether the tool truly helps.
S0.quote: I can afford a short experiment with my time, not a careless job change.
fieldNote: She already uses **AI daily** but verifies omitted complaint details.
Her **four-month reserve** gives room for a measured experiment.
She judges the tool by **customer scores**, not novelty alone.

steps.text: Use the approved AI tool to summarise routine chats
Coach agents on difficult cases during the saved time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues the easy chat queue may shrink and we should claim time for the tougher cases. I'd rather help design the new workflow than wait for it to arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I think management could keep one experienced lead and stop hiring juniors. I might be that lead, but I don't want my whole career resting on a single seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll document errors in the current bot replies and test a better handoff with the team. I'll add part of each paycheque to savings to keep four months of expenses covered. In the first year, if a paid workflow-review vacancy opens at either local centre, I'll apply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious but busy. I see a route, yet I can also see the headcount dropping.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the new handoff?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask two agents to test whether the bot passes the caller's actual problem to us. We would take the results to the team meeting rather than saying the tool feels good or bad.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What pay would make a move worthwhile?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would need a posted wage at least as good as this lead job. A shiny title with less take-home pay would use up my buffer slowly.

say: I'd ask for **more time** on complex calls after easy chats shrink.
I'd volunteer to **test handoffs** with the team.
think: I might keep the **lead seat**, but I cannot build a career on one opening.
do: Test **bot handoffs** with two agents this month.
Apply for a **posted paid review job** if the wage matches.
Add **monthly pay** to keep four months of expenses saved.
feel: **Anxious** about fewer seats, while still seeing a possible route.
S1.quote: A shiny title with less take-home pay would use up my buffer slowly.
fieldNote: She sees **design work** as a possible move, not a guaranteed post.
Her **team test** produces evidence from real calls.
She protects her **pay floor** despite enthusiasm for the technology.

steps.text: Test bot handoffs on real calls with two agents
Apply for posted paid workflow-review vacancies at matching pay
Add monthly pay to maintain four months of expenses saved

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say our centre cannot pretend 2028 general AI is just a better chat bot. Calls and chats are the first work it could do; robots around 2031 come later for other jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my present role could disappear, including the parts where I solve unusual cases. Four months saved gives me a runway, but if every centre buys the same system, the nearby jobs might close together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From now I'll build a portfolio of failed bot handoffs and the fixes I made, without customer details. If my post is cut in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for posted paid service-audit jobs and use the savings to cover rent while I search; I won't quit on a forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm anxious, and I can feel that in my stomach. I have a plan and some time, but I cannot guarantee a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would review your portfolio?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show my former flatmate from college the anonymised examples and ask whether they make sense outside a call centre. That is feedback, not a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the manager?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my manager which audit tasks still have people assigned and what they pay. If there is no posted job, I'll keep drawing my current wage for as long as the role exists.

say: I'd tell the centre **2028 AGI** could handle calls, not just easy chats.
I'd explain **2031 robots** do not extend our phone-work deadline.
think: I expect my **lead role** could disappear.
I fear **nearby centres** could shrink together despite my four-month reserve.
do: Build an **anonymised handoff portfolio** starting now.
Apply for **posted paid audit jobs** after a real cut.
Use **savings for rent** during an actual job search.
feel: **Anxious** because she has a plan but cannot guarantee a vacancy.
S2.quote: Four months saved gives me a runway, but if every centre buys the same system, the nearby jobs might close together.
fieldNote: She accepts her **own role** may go despite high skill.
Her **portfolio** protects customer details and proves work she actually did.
She will **stay employed** until an actual cut or paid alternative appears.

steps.text: Apply for posted paid service-audit jobs if her role is cut
Keep drawing her centre wage while the role exists

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team five years is long enough to build the review job in public, with pay and training attached. Our calls face general AI in 2031, well before hands-on robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could use five years to become genuinely good at checking service systems, not just making slide decks about them. I still worry the centre might remove junior seats before the formal AGI date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask for paid time to run a monthly audit of bot handoffs, and if it is approved I'll complete the service-testing course the centre offers. Before 2031 I'll apply for posted paid review roles when their wages match mine; in the first year after AGI arrives, I'll stay in whichever paid role I have while checking the new openings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Focused, with some unease. The work could become interesting, but people beside me may lose hours first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would junior agents get a place in the reviews?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would include a junior agent in each monthly review so they learn how we find mistakes. That only works if the centre pays them for the time too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I won't pay a large fee out of my rent reserve. If the centre will not fund the course and audit hours, I'll practise on approved tools during my ordinary shift instead.

say: I'd ask for **paid review work** during the five-year window.
I'd warn that **2034 robots** do not delay changes to calls in 2031.
think: I could gain **real testing skill** over five years.
I worry **junior hours** could shrink before formal AGI arrives.
do: Run **monthly handoff audits** only with approved paid time.
Complete the **service-testing course** only with centre funding and paid study hours.
Apply for **posted wage-matched review roles** before 2031.
feel: **Focused**, while uneasy about junior colleagues losing hours.
S3.quote: I won't pay a large fee out of my rent reserve.
fieldNote: Her **training plan** requires funded course and paid audit hours.
She includes **junior agents** only when their time is paid.
She sees **early hour cuts** as possible before the stated AGI arrival.

steps.text: Complete centre-funded service-testing course only with paid study hours
Apply for posted paid review roles at matching wages
Run monthly bot-handoff audits during approved paid hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade gives us time to build a different service career and insist the centre trains people properly. General AI in 2036 hits the calls; robots around 2039 are not the clock I watch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can imagine leaving the headset before 2036 by choice, perhaps for service design. I still want a posted role and a wage, not a beautiful plan with no employer behind it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my lead shift and spend one approved hour each week testing the customer handoff. Over the decade I'll compare paid service-design vacancies every six months; in the first year after 2036, I'll move only if an actual opening pays enough to cover my flat and lets me use that experience.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Curious and calm. The extra years give me room to build evidence instead of gambling my savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What proof would you carry to an interview?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep a dated record of what a customer asked and where the handoff failed, with names removed. That is better proof of skill than saying I am enthusiastic about AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the agents you train?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the agents I train to learn during paid hours while they keep earning. A long forecast is a reason to learn in paid hours, not to leave today. They still need this month's wages.

say: I'd ask for **paid learning time** across the decade.
I'd focus on **2036 call work**, not 2039 robots.
think: I could leave the **headset by choice** before 2036.
I still need a **posted wage** behind any service-design plan.
do: Keep my **lead shift** through the coming year.
Test **customer handoffs** for one approved paid hour weekly.
Compare **paid design vacancies** twice yearly and move only if wages cover my flat.
feel: **Curious and calm** with time to build proof.
S4.quote: A long forecast is a reason to learn in paid hours, not to leave today.
fieldNote: She treats the **ten-year window** as time to build evidence, not a cue to resign.
Her **weekly test** happens only in approved paid time.
She keeps a **wage threshold** tied to the cost of her flat.

steps.text: Keep leading the contact-centre shift this year
Test customer handoffs during approved paid weekly hours
Compare posted paid design vacancies and move only if wages cover rent

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because local centres might all cut at once. My four months saved is a runway, not a new career. Paid audit vacancies, honest notice and training during paid hours would make the search possible.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the customer whether the handoff made sense. We can admire a clever system from inside the centre and still leave a person repeating their story three times. I would measure that before counting saved minutes.

headlineQuote: We can admire a clever system from inside the centre and still leave a person repeating their story three times.
portrait: Wendy is a **27-year-old lead** handling phone and chat cases, with a two-year college diploma and strong service skills.
She earns **typical pay**, rents alone and has four months saved; some comparable centres sit nearby.
She uses **AI daily** and tests tools against actual customer handoffs while protecting a wage that covers her flat.
The **2028 picture** worries her most; a longer runway lets her build paid audit skill and seek posted roles.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink several nearby centres at once and overwhelm her four-month reserve.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid audit vacancies** would turn her handoff work into a possible next job.
**Paid training time** and honest notice would let her prepare without using rent savings.
